title: Chapter 7: Post-Incident Activity Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of lessons learned, reporting, evidence retention, and continuous improvement.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of the Post-Incident Activity phase?
options: To restore systems to normal operation.
To learn from the incident and improve future response.
To contain the spread of malware.
To identify the initial attack vector.
questions.explanation: Post-Incident focuses on organizational learning, documentation, and process improvement.

questions.question: A Lessons Learned meeting should focus on blaming the individual who made the mistake to ensure accountability.
questions.explanation: False. It should be 'blameless' and focus on systemic process failures.

questions.question: Who is the most appropriate person to facilitate a Lessons Learned meeting?
questions.explanation: The Incident Commander has the full context and leadership skills to guide the discussion effectively.

questions.question: The 'Five Whys' technique is used to identify the ______ cause of a problem.
questions.explanation: Five Whys drills past symptoms to find the underlying process or technical failure.

questions.question: Which audience is the 'Executive Summary' report written for?
questions.explanation: The Executive Summary translates technical events into business impact (money, risk, reputation).

questions.question: Detailed technical IOCs (IP addresses, file hashes) belong in the Executive Summary.
questions.explanation: False. Technical details belong in the Technical Incident Report, not the Executive Summary.

questions.question: Under GDPR, within how many hours must a supervisory authority be notified of a personal data breach?
questions.explanation: GDPR Article 33 requires notification within 72 hours of awareness.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a Chain of Custody form?
options: To track the financial cost of evidence.
To prove evidence has not been tampered with and is admissible in court.
To list the contents of a forensic image.
questions.explanation: Chain of Custody ensures integrity and legal admissibility.

questions.question: A Litigation Hold (Legal Hold) overrides standard data retention policies and prevents deletion of evidence.
questions.explanation: True. A hold suspends normal deletion processes to preserve evidence for legal proceedings.

questions.question: What is a 'SMART' Action Item?
options: An action item that is completed quickly.
An action item that is Specific, Measurable, Assignable, Realistic, and Time-bound.
An action item assigned to the smartest person on the team.
An action item that requires no follow-up.
questions.explanation: SMART criteria ensure action items are clear and trackable.

questions.question: The final phase of the Incident Response lifecycle feeds directly back into the ______ phase.
questions.explanation: Lessons learned update policies, playbooks, and tools—all part of Preparation.

questions.question: Which metric tracks the average time from detection to containment?
questions.explanation: MTTR = Mean Time to Respond/Remediate. MTTD = Mean Time to Detect.

questions.question: Evidence (disk images, memory dumps) should be deleted immediately after the incident is resolved to save storage space.
questions.explanation: False. Retention is often required for months or years due to legal and insurance obligations.

questions.question: What is the best method to verify that a forensic image file has not been altered since acquisition?
options: Open the file and look at it.
Compare the current cryptographic hash to the acquisition hash.
questions.explanation: Cryptographic hashes (MD5, SHA256) are the standard for integrity verification.

questions.question: Why is it important to include 'What Worked Well' in a Lessons Learned meeting?
options: To fill time in the meeting.
To boost team morale and reinforce positive behaviors.
questions.explanation: Celebrating wins acknowledges team effort and encourages repetition of successful actions.

questions.question: The 'Parking Lot' technique is used to manage off-topic discussions during a Lessons Learned meeting.
questions.explanation: True. It captures valid but off-agenda points for later discussion without derailing the current meeting.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid section in a Technical Incident Report?
questions.explanation: MITRE ATT&CK mapping provides a standardized way to describe adversary behavior in technical reports.

questions.question: WORM storage stands for Write-Once-______-Many.
questions.explanation: WORM prevents modification or deletion of data for a specified retention period.

questions.question: A recurring incident with the same root cause indicates a failure in which phase?
questions.explanation: If the same issue happens again, the Lessons Learned process failed to implement effective corrective actions.

questions.question: Celebrating team success after an incident is an optional, 'nice to have' activity with no impact on future performance.
questions.explanation: False. Recognition and morale are critical for retaining skilled responders and maintaining team cohesion under pressure.
